correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the theorem for the specified unweighted GP(8,3). Distance signatures separate all vertices exactly when the indicated subset is resolving; enumeration of sizes 0 through 4 proves minimality and completeness. A legal move is uniquely specified by the removed and inserted vertices of two distinct sets differing in one element, with the extra adjacency predicate for a slide. Exhaustive unweighted shortest-path searches and comparison of the two distance matrices therefore exhaust all 51,040 unordered pairs. A fresh independent program reproduced zero smaller sets, 320 bases, the full degree, eccentricity, distance and penalty distributions, both connected graphs, the two radii and diameters, and the distances (2,10) for the stated witness. It enumerated 96 automorphisms, with orbit sizes 24,24,32,48,96,96. Preservation of adjacency and nonadjacency is a sound pruning condition on partial injections and characterizes automorphisms on completed bijections. The recorded GP and LCF checks corroborate but do not substitute for the fresh run.
residual_risks: The exhaustion is for minimum-cardinality ordinary vertex-resolving sets of this one graph, not minimal sets of arbitrary size, weak-total or edge metric bases, labeled tokens, or intermediate nonbases.
The proof wording about sixteen-component signatures can be read as a transposition: each of sixteen vertices has a four-component landmark signature. The check uses that correct predicate.

value.rationale: The canonical symmetric cubic graph gives a useful complete example of how local moves alter the geometry of all optimal landmark placements. The two graphs are both connected, yet sliding makes every state have eccentricity 12 while jumping has two eccentricity classes and diameter 5. The exact optimal penalty and explicit witness measure the loss from locality instead of just comparing diameters or exhibiting one feasible route. The complete census includes the orbit classification on which future symmetry-based comparisons can build; it is not merely a recomputation of the metric dimension.
residual_risks: A natural finite benchmark, not an asserted scaling law or reconfiguration theorem for all symmetric cubic graphs.
